R0078.title: Data Breach
R0078.definition: Data breach risk refers to the potential threat of an organization's or individual's sensitive, confidential, or personally identifiable information being disclosed, exposed, or accessed without authorization.
R0078.description: May occur in various scenarios, including cyberattacks, insider leaks, and physical device loss or theft.
R0078.influence: Harms include privacy violations, financial losses, legal liability, and reputational damage, potentially causing serious impacts on both organizations and individuals.

observables: Databases or object storage show unauthorized bulk exports or anomalous queries
Sale listings closely matching this organization's data characteristics appear on the dark web or public channels
Internal accounts anomalously access sensitive tables or fields unrelated to their duties
Data is transmitted to unauthorized external addresses, with DLP rules alerting frequently

R0078-001.title: Partner Data Breach
R0078-001.definition: Sensitive information leakage caused by external entities or service providers that partner with the organization, due to insufficient security measures, technical vulnerabilities, or improper operations when handling, storing, or transmitting data.
R0078-001.description: Common scenarios for partner data breaches include third-party service providers being attacked, partner APIs being called beyond authorization, data-transmission links lacking encryption or access control, and partner personnel accounts being compromised. Because organizations lack direct control over the security posture of external entities, partners often become a springboard for attackers to reach the organization's data assets; breach incidents often involve customer privacy, trade secrets, and compliance data, triggering trust crises and regulatory penalties.
R0078-001.influence: Harms include loss of trust from customers and business partners, legal liability, reputational damage, and potential financial losses, posing potential threats to both the organization and its partners.

observables: After a partner or third-party system is breached, this organization's data is leaked on the dark web or public channels
Partner API calls exceed the agreed scope, anomalously pulling this organization's sensitive data
Data-transmission links to partners lack encryption or access control and are intercepted by man-in-the-middle actors
Partner personnel accounts are compromised and used to access this organization's shared data beyond their authorization

R0078-002.title: Customer Success and Support Ticket Data Exposure
R0078-002.definition: Customer privacy data, keys, screenshots, and business information in support, CRM, or ticket systems are accessed or exported without authorization.
R0078-002.description:
Customer success and support ticket data exposure comes from CRM, support systems, ticketing platforms, and collaboration tools that contain chats, screenshots, secrets, account data, and business context. Data can be accessed or exported beyond authorization.

Support teams need broad visibility to solve issues, but excessive permissions and outsourced collaboration increase leakage. Controls need field masking, tiered access, export control, and sensitive ticket auditing.
R0078-002.influence: Support ticket exposure can leak customer privacy, business screenshots, secrets, and incident details, damaging trust and compliance.

observables: Support or CRM accounts anomalously bulk-export tickets, customer chat logs, screenshots, or keys
Outsourced support accounts access customer privacy data beyond their service scope without authorization
Ticket-system export volume surges outside working hours, with exported fields containing sensitive information
Support accounts exfiltrate ticket screenshots or customer credentials via collaboration tools

R0078-003.title: User Privacy Leakage
R0078-003.definition: User privacy leakage (PII leaked) refers to the potential threat to personal sensitive information stored, processed, or transmitted on a platform due to security vulnerabilities, data breaches, or misuse, causing user privacy and security issues.
R0078-003.description: Causes of personal privacy leakage risk include platform security vulnerabilities, unauthorized data access, misuse of user data, and improper handling of user information by third-party partners, all of which create potential risks of user privacy exposure.
R0078-003.influence: Personal privacy leakage risk may cause users to lose trust, trigger legal liability, damage the platform's reputation, reduce user activity, and create regulatory compliance issues, negatively impacting the platform's sustainable development.

observables: User PII data is exposed in plaintext on unauthorized interfaces or in logs
Third-party partners improperly call user-data interfaces, pulling volumes beyond the authorized scope
Platform security vulnerabilities cause user privacy data to be probed in bulk or scraped via database dumping
Datasets matching the platform's user characteristics appear on the dark web
